events.title: The Robert Cray Band
events.summary: The Robert Cray Band performs live at Buffalo State Performing Arts Center November 3 as part of their All Amped Up Tour
events.description: The Buffalo State Performing Arts Center presents The Robert Cray Band: All Amped Up Tour on Tuesday, November 3 at 7:30 p.m. Blues icon. Soul man. Rock and roller. Robert Cray is all these things–and more. From forming a teenage garage band to striding the stage alongside several of the world’s greatest guitarists, Cray has sold millions of albums and countless concert tickets, won five Grammy Awards, been inducted into the Blues Hall of Fame and the recipient of the Americana Music Lifetime Achievement Award, and has designed two signature model Fender guitars—but for him, what’s always mattered most is the music. Cray has shared stage and/or studio with the likes of Muddy Waters, B.B. King, Buddy Guy, Chuck Berry, The Rolling Stones, Eric Clapton, Tina Turner, Stevie Ray Vaughan and more. In 1978, he was cast (as a musician) in Animal House, the blockbuster comedy that made John Belushi famous. 1978 was also the year Cray recorded his debut album, Who’s Been Talkin’. Cray’s 1983 album Bad Influence established him internationally, and his 1986 album, Strong Persuader—released after he’d signed with Mercury Records—ensured he became the first blues/soul musician to breakthrough in the MTV era. That album led to Cray gracing the cover of Rolling Stone magazine, winning the Grammy for Best Contemporary Blues Recording in 1988, and supporting Tina Turner by joining her on stage every night and touring with The Rolling Stone. Across five decades, Cray has created richly inclusive American music, revitalizing both blues and soul while rocking hard with the very best. To achieve 50 years in the music industry and still be as fresh and committed as when starting out is an achievement few can boast of, but Cray can count himself among those few. He has released 19 studio albums, every one replete with extremely distinctive songs, won five Grammy Awards, and continues to make music that sounds like no one but Robert Cray.

events.title: Terrance Simien and The Zydeco Experience presented by the Susquehanna University Artist Series
events.summary: Two-time Grammy Award winners, Terrance Simien and The Zydeco Experience come to Susquehanna University as some of the most respected and accomplished artists in American roots music today.
events.artists: Terrance Simien and The Zydeco Experience
events.keywords: music, livemusic, rock, r&b, folk
events.description:
At its roots, Zydeco was an acoustic tradition built around the accordion, fiddle and triangle, with songs sung in French. Early generations simply called it French music. Before that, its origins can the traced to the 19th century call-and response juré songs, performed with little more than clapping hands, stomping feet and “the yearning” — often voices of the oppressed French-speaking Black people of Louisiana. For over 40 years, two-time Grammy Award–winning, eighth-generation Louisiana Creole musician Terrance Simien has carried the tradition forward with his acclaimed Zydeco Experience band. Widely regarded as one of America’s foremost roots musicians, Simien has helped introduce Zydeco to audiences across the globe while honoring its rich cultural heritage. The band’s music has been featured in major studio films, including Disney’s The Princess and the Frog, as well as television programs and radio commercials. They have performed in over 45 countries and, since the mid-1980s, have served as cultural ambassadors on U.S. Department of State cultural diplomacy tours.
Tickets can be obtained online at https://susqu.universitytickets.com/ 
Box Office hours: Mon-Fri, 12pm – 5pm; closed during breaks; 570-372-ARTS

events.title: UB40
events.summary: UB40 is one of the most successful and influential British groups of all time, with more than 100 million albums sold, and more than 50 charting singles in the UK.
events.keywords: foxtucsontheatre, ub40
events.description:
UB40 is one of the most successful and influential British groups of all time, with more than 100 million albums sold, and more than 50 charting singles in the UK, including their trademark global #1 hits “Red Red Wine” and “(I Can’t Help) Falling in Love With You”; and U.S. Top 10s “Here I Am (Come and Take Me)” and “The Way You Do The Things You Do.” The reggae/pop legends set the stage this fall for their highly anticipated Relentless tour, performing their iconic hit songs, along with new songs and reworked classics from their recently released hit 45th Anniversary album, UB45, which reached #5 on the UK official album chart. The nine-piece ensemble’s 2025 tour includes on select dates, The English Beat, Inner Circle and Big Mountain.

“For more than 40 years, we’ve been one of the hardest working touring bands in pop music,” says guitarist/vocalist and UB40 co- founder Robin Campbell, who along with Jimmy Brown (drums), Earl Falconer (bass, vocals) and Norman Hassan (percussion, trombone, vocals), have been the core of the band for its entire ever-evolving history. “We aim to have a party every show. As much as we’ve enjoyed our Zoom chats during lockdown, there’s no substitute for the relationship and synergy we have with our live audiences.”

Lead singer Matt Doyle joined the band in 2021 when he was a member of the popular Birmingham reggae band KIOKO – taking over for Duncan Campbell, UB40’s lead singer since 2008 who retired after suffering a stroke. UB40 first got wind of the magic Doyle brings to the stage as a singer and performer when KIOKO opened for them in 2018 at The Royal Albert Hall and supported UB40 on their subsequent UK and European tours. Says Campbell, “Watching Matt standing there in the middle of the stage like a rabbit in headlights, full of shock and awe that he’s playing with a band he loved growing up, was simply fantastic but now his confidence has grown and he’s settled into the job with consummate ease.”

For Doyle, naturally, it’s beyond a dream to be in those proverbial headlights. “Everyone has been so warm and welcoming,” he says, “and I’ve received so many beautiful wishes from fans from around the world, saying I’m the perfect guy for the job and they can’t wait to see me perform. Not only is it amazing being with the band singing these incredible songs I grew up with, but it’s also a blast sitting in a room just listening to these guys with so much worldwide touring experience tell their stories. KIOKO were doing very well, and

I’m grateful for my time with them which allowed me to find my voice and hone my craft. But joining UB40 is like jumping on a ladder and climbing straight to the top floor.”

In addition to Doyle, Campbell, Brown, Falconer and Hassan, UB40’s current lineup includes long time members Martin Meredith (saxophone/WX7/ keyboards), and Laurence Parry (trumpet/ flugal trombone), IanThompson (saxophone) and newest member Jahred Gordon (keyboards), backing vocalist Matt Campbell plus permanent guest emcee Gilly G.

2023 marked UB40’s 45th year as a band, and they celebrated with further shows including an emotional sold out Royal Albert Hall and a summer return to the US. They’ve continued their 45th celebrations by recording a new album which is out on the 19th of April 2024, the album – UB45 – consists of seven brand new songs and seven re-recordings of some classic UB40, a mixture of originals and Labour of Love songs. UB40’s 45 year celebrations will continue well into 2024. Following the release of UB45, the band will embark on a massive headline arena tour of the UK and Europe.

Robin Campbell said: “We’re so proud of this album and the new songs, but we also wanted to showcase Matt Doyle’s vocals on some of the classics because he does them so well. He’s brought a new lease of life to our music, as has fellow Brummie “permanent guest” MC Gilly G. When you play songs over so many years, the arrangements and vocals evolve and change. These updated versions of our hits are still close to the originals, but now reflect how we perform them today and to me they sound better than ever”.

“We continue to make albums for the simple reason that we love doing it and we’re forever inspired by the reactions of our multiple generations of fans,” says Campbell. “Playing ‘Red Red Wine’ and having thousands of people sing back to us every night is fantastic, but we never want to become a cabaret act or do a Vegas residency where we only play decades-old hits for nostalgia’s sake. There’s always an incredible buzz when we present new material and get the stamp of approval from the audience.

events.title: Necessary Turbulence: Fifty Years, One Unbreakable Sisterhood
events.summary: Join us for a panel discussion of decorated officers and contributing authors for Necessary Turbulence: Fifty Years, One Unbreakable Sisterhood Forged in the Crucible of the Air Force Academy.
events.description:
Tickets for this event are $5 general admission or book purchase. 

Join us for a panel discussion of decorated officers and contributing authors for Necessary Turbulence: Fifty Years, One Unbreakable Sisterhood Forged in the Crucible of the Air Force Academy. Our guest speakers are all graduates from the U.S. Air Force Academy, classes 1991–2006, who have served their country as doctors, professors, and pilots. They are now local leaders in medicine, consultancy, higher education, commercial aviation, and nonprofit work, as well as passionate volunteers deeply invested in our Central Oregon community. It’s a chance to learn, connect, and hear about their unique experiences stemming from a shared sisterhood.

For fifty years, an extraordinary story has been hiding in plain sight.

This book is carried by the lives of 108 women.

They did not move through history together.
They did not follow the same paths.
They did not arrive at the same destinations.

What connects them is not outcome or identity, but a shared beginning—and a shared willingness to shoulder commitment and duty early, then carry it forward across a lifetime of leadership.

Theirs is the definitive account of fifty years that changed everything.​

Necessary Turbulence is a collective narrative of women who came of age inside systems that were not built for them and learned, in real time, how to live, lead, and redefine themselves anyway. In 1976, 157 young women marched beneath the words "Bring Me Men" at the top of a ramp leading into a world that had never imagined them. They, and the more than 12,000 who followed, faced a contentious culture, inadequate facilities, and a system designed to break them. Told they were destroying standards and would never graduate, more than 7,000 women proved them wrong.

Drawn from 108 voices across five decades, this narrative traces what it meant to begin without a roadmap: to enter environments where expectations were unclear, belonging was not guaranteed, and the cost of getting it wrong was high. It chronicles women learning to navigate pressure, claim authority, and build lives of consequence.

Panelists include:

Lt Col Carlene Perry, USAF (Retired)

Lt Col Torree McGowan, USAF Medical Corps (Retired)

Lt Col Lisa (Jorgensen) Christensen, USAF (Retired)

Captain Kristin (Hamlett) Berg, USAF (Veteran)

Lt Col MaxieJane Frazier, USAF (Retired)

events.title: Dolly's Clinic
events.summary: Immersive art exhibition presenting animal sculptures as patients in aesthetics clinic
events.keywords: contemporaryart, sculpture, womanartist, cosmeticsurgery, beauty, multimedia, fitzrovia
events.description:
Presented off-site by Mandy Zhang Art and guest curated by Joséphine May Bailey, Dolly’s Clinic places Annie Trevorah’s enquiry into aesthetics, bodily modification and the politics of appearance in context of medieval bestiaries and surrealist imaginations.

Referencing the language and rituals of the contemporary beauty industry, Trevorah introduces a meticulously realised aesthetics clinic for animals named after the first cloned mammal. A cast of six matte aluminium sculptures, each enhanced with organic elements, model a range of signature procedures, complete with consultant’s notes and recovery plans. An interactive AR visualisation by multimedia artist Dr Blanca Regina invites viewers to join an exfoliated poodle’s celebration of its smooth new body.

Beneath a playful and humorous surface, the exhibition raises fundamental questions about humanity’s relationship with other species. With Dolly’s Clinic Annie Trevorah challenges the assumption that humans alone possess the authority to determine how other living beings should look, function and evolve, while exploring the contradictions between personal freedoms and external pressures.

Tuesday-Friday, 10am – 6pm, Saturday, 11am – 6pm

events.title: "No one should feel alone” – Whitstable care home invites community to friendship café
events.summary: A care home in Whitstable is inviting people to build new friendships with their neighbours this autumn.

Care UK’s Harrier Lodge, on Thanet Way, is opening its doors to residents of Whitstable and surrounding areas for to its Friendship Café on Wednesday 4th November, from 10.30am–11.30am, as part of their permanent community hub at the home. 

On the first Wednesday of every month, local people are encouraged to visit the home’s café and enjoy hot drinks and freshly baked treats in good company. The café is open to anyone who wishes to make new friends and chat with residents, team members and other community members in a relaxed environment.  

Susan Simmonds, Home Manager at Harrier Lodge, said: “We think these events are a lovely way to have a positive impact on our community, and support anyone who may be feeling lonely. 

“Building support systems is extremely important, and we are committed to helping local people understand the help and expertise available at our Friendship Café – a space where everyone is able to relax and enjoy themselves.  

“We’re looking forward to welcoming local people and meeting some new faces while enjoying a chat over a cup of tea and slice of cake.” 

Harrier Lodge is a purpose-built care home that has been designed to enable residents to lead active and fulfilled lives, while also promoting independence. The expert team provides full-time residential, nursing and specialist dementia care for up to 65 older people in Whitstable. The stunning home incorporates plenty of space for leisure activities and hobbies, including its own cinema, hair and beauty salon, and pub.
